binders: A format fmt determined by β,p∈ℕ and emin,emax∈ℤ, with 2≤β, 0<p, and emin≤emax.
Three scalar real inputs x1, x2, and x3.
A witness run that this trace satisfies the structured represented, rounded, split, bounded, and no-overflow computation conditions described below.
hypotheses: Let βR=↑β, S(e)=βR^e for e∈ℤ, B=βR^p, A=↑(β^p-1), C=↑(β^p-(β div 2)), and MaxValue=A·S(emax); the operations inside A and C are natural-number operations.
A representation of x consists of m,e∈ℤ satisfying -B<↑m<B, emin≤e≤emax, and x=(↑m)S(e). A canonical representation is one whose exponent is no larger than that of every representation of the same x.
Nearest(x,q) means q is representable and |x-q|≤|x-c| for every representable real c. Ties are permitted.

For canonical operand representations and supplied grids gL,gR, Split(L,R;gL,gR;H,L0) means: H and L0 have canonical representations; Nearest(LR,H); H+L0=LR; LR≠0 implies H≠0; |L0|≤(B/2)S(gL+gR); |LR|≤MaxValue; and |L0|≤(1/2)S(eH), where eH is the exponent of the stored canonical representation of H.
The run supplies canonical representations of x1,x2,x3, with exponents e1,e2,e3.
The run contains Split(x2,x3;e2,e3;th,tl). If eh is the exponent of the resulting canonical representation of th, it also contains Split(x1,th;e1,eh;s1,a2) and Split(x1,tl;e1,e2+e3;a3,a4).
The run assumes Nearest(a2+a3,s2), Nearest(s2-a2,t), and Nearest(a3-t,r).
conclusions: There exist integers m and e such that -B<↑m<B, emin≤e≤emax, a2=(↑m)S(e), and |a3|≤C·S(e), where C=↑(β^p-(β div 2)).
mathematical_definitions: All x-values, trace components, products, sums, residuals, and rounded values are scalar real numbers; there are no vector or matrix dimensions.
The only magnitude function in the proposition is the ordinary real absolute value |·|, not a separately parameterized norm.
The scale uses integer powers, so S(e)=βR^e also covers negative exponents.
Representability is the existence of a bounded integer mantissa and bounded integer exponent satisfying an exact real equality.
The product-split relations include both exact decompositions and nearest-rounding assertions; the target's final equality is an exact real identity.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every admissible radix-β format, every three real inputs, every ten-real trace, and every witness that the trace arises from the specified sequence of canonical representations, nearest-rounded product splits, compensated merge operations, residual bounds, and no-overflow conditions, a2 has some bounded radix representation whose exponent e makes |a3| no greater than ↑(β^p-(β div 2))·βR^e. Moreover, the rounded merge and final addition are exact in the stated places: t=s2-a2, r=a3-t, s2+r=a2+a3, and s3=r+a4; consequently the accumulated value (s1+s2)+s3 equals the exact real product (x1x2)x3.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is universal over a run witness. For any fmt, inputs, and trace admitting no such witness, the statement has no applicable run instance and is vacuous.

Existence of run is highly restrictive: it requires canonical representations for all inputs and product components, nearest-rounding witnesses, exact split equations, residual bounds, and several no-overflow inequalities.

The first conclusion does not identify its representation of a2 with a particular representation stored in run; it only asserts that some representation of a2 satisfies the stronger exponent-dependent bound.
Canonical means minimal exponent among representations, not a unique representation. Multiple representations or canonical witnesses may exist.
Nearest rounding permits ties and encodes no tie-breaking rule, rounding mode beyond nearest, or deterministic rounding function.
The coefficient C is based on natural quotient β div 2 and natural subtraction: it is ↑(β^p-floor(β/2)), not βR^p-βR/2.
The model uses exact real numbers and a bespoke finite representation set. It does not encode NaNs, infinities, signed zero, subnormal-specific behavior, flags, or hardware evaluation semantics.
No conclusion independently asserts existence of a run for every input triple or format.
No vector, matrix, probabilistic, or asymptotic statement is present.
